chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Zakariyya Al-Saydalani, from a man from the Banu Hanifa, from the people of Bust and Sajistan, who said:

I accompanied Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the year in which he performed Hajj during the beginning of the caliphate of Al-Mu'tasim. So I said to him while I was with him at the meal, and there was a group from the governors of the Sultan: 'Our governor is a man who befriends you, O People of the Household, and loves you. And a tax is levied on me in his office. So if you see fit, may I be sacrificed for you, write to him a letter of favor for me.' He said to me: 'I do not know him.'

So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, he is upon what I said regarding his love for you, O People of the Household, and your letter will benefit me with him.' So he took the paper and wrote: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. As for what follows, the bearer of this letter of mine has mentioned about you a beautiful doctrine, and that what is for you from your work is what you have done well in it. So be good to your brethren, and know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will question you about the weight of particles and mustard seeds.'

He (the narrator) said: So when I arrived in Sajistan, the news preceded to Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Naysaburi, and he was the governor. So he welcomed me two farsakhs from the city. So I handed over the letter to him. He kissed it and placed it on his eyes, then said to me: 'What is your need?' So I said: 'A tax is levied on me in your office.'

He said: So he ordered for the tax to be removed from me and said to me: 'You will not pay any tax as long as I have authority.' Then he asked me about my dependents, so I informed him of their number. So he ordered for me and for them with what would provide for us and extra. So I did not pay any tax during his term in office as long as he was alive, and he did not cut off my connection (favor) until he died.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam's letter influence the governor's treatment of the narrator?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical political influence of the Imams during the Abbasid era, specifically under Caliph al-Mu'tasim, where a brief epistle could secure significant fiscal relief. The Imam’s concise letter emphasizes *al-mithaqil al-dharr* (divine accountability for minute deeds), a key Shia theological concept linking administrative justice to spiritual responsibility. The narrative highlights the efficacy of the Imam’s word in securing rights for the faithful within the existing bureaucratic structure, serving as a model for leveraging religious authority in worldly affairs.
